content.value_statement: Training runs often lose command, log, and checkpoint context. This skill runs a selected command and records bounded evidence in train_outputs.
actual_capabilities: Executes a selected training command with a configurable timeout.
Captures stdout, stderr, return code, and timeout status.
Parses logs for epochs, steps, metrics, and checkpoint file names.
Records git status differences before and after execution.
Produces normalized status data for train_outputs bundles.
limitations: Does not select research goals or training commands.
Does not install environments or download assets.
Does not run exploratory sweeps or speculative architecture changes.
Can execute arbitrary user-provided commands, so use only in trusted repositories.

use_cases.title: Verify Training Startup
use_cases.description: Run a selected command briefly and confirm that logs, steps, and blockers are captured.

use_cases.title: Resume a Known Run
use_cases.description: Start from a chosen checkpoint and record whether the resume path works as expected.

use_cases.title: Collect Reproduction Evidence
use_cases.description: Create a bounded report of command, metrics, checkpoints, and changed files for review.

prompt_templates.title: Run Startup Verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Run startup verification for this selected training command: <command>. Use a 120 second timeout and summarize the evidence in train_outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Short Run
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a short-run verification for <command> with dataset assumptions: <dataset>. Capture steps, metrics, logs, and checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Resume From Checkpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume training with <command> from <checkpoint>. Record whether resume started correctly and identify any blocker.

prompt_templates.title: Kick Off Trusted Training
prompt_templates.prompt: Kick off trusted full training with <command>. Monitor for <minutes> minutes, then record status, changed files, and reproducibility evidence.

output_examples.input: Startup verification for a selected training command with a 120 second window.
output_examples.output: The run started, reached step 12, found no checkpoint yet, and recorded a partial status with captured logs.

output_examples.input: Resume verification from a named checkpoint.
output_examples.output: The resume command launched successfully, reported the checkpoint path, and stopped after the planned monitoring window.

output_examples.input: Short-run verification after a nonzero exit.
output_examples.output: The report marks the run as partial, preserves stderr evidence, and lists the training command exit code as the blocker.

best_practices: Provide the exact selected command and expected run mode.
Set a short timeout before a full kickoff.
Review generated logs and status before treating results as reproduced.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to choose research ideas or sweep variants.
Do not run untrusted commands or repositories through this skill.
Do not treat startup verification as full reproduction success.

faq.question: Does this skill choose the training command?
faq.answer: No. It expects a selected command and runs it conservatively.

faq.question: Can it run full training?
faq.answer: Yes, but only as a trusted kickoff with bounded monitoring and clear status reporting.

faq.question: What evidence does it collect?
faq.answer: It captures logs, return status, metrics, checkpoints, changed files, and runtime assumptions when available.

faq.question: Does startup verification prove reproduction success?
faq.answer: No. Startup verification only shows that the command starts and produces early evidence.

faq.question: Can it install missing dependencies?
faq.answer: No. Environment setup and asset downloads are outside this skill scope.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted repositories?
faq.answer: No. It can execute local commands, so use it only with trusted code and explicit approval.
